translations.title: As the Nile Conceals Its Source
translations.text:
Happy are you, O Nile, born unwitnessed and of unknown parents, cloud and river, making tree and wheat fertile.


The moisture the raging Dog drinks thirstily from sacred rivers he lavishly adds to your fords, Aquarius becoming Leo for you.


No otherwise, Lisis, does it happen to the watery urns of my eyes, whose unknown source remains unspoken.


For when the Sirius of your red bonds burns in blushes of fresh gold, their flood, your ice, and my grief increase.
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly for batch completion; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: This Metal, Blazing Bright
translations.text:
This metal, blazing bright and holding so much envy in so little bulk, renounced the earth among the flames and no longer knows the crag as kin.


Melted, it displays an almighty arm: terror lent by the mountain to the city, pallid peace, costly war, poison of dawn and sunset.


Cut into harsh coins, this little globe rivals man in claiming to be the world abridged.


Pale law permitting everything, wealth more lost the more it is guarded, thirst that abundance cannot allay.
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly for batch completion; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: Life Begins with Tears and Shit...
translations.text:
Life begins with tears and shit; then come moo, mama, and boogeyman; then smallpox, drool, and snot, then the top and rattle.


As one grows come the girlfriend and her coaxing; mad appetite attacks with her; in youth nothing suffices, and afterward desire sins like a rogue.


He becomes a man and muddles everything; single, he chases every skirt; married, he turns a nasty cuckold.


Old, he grays, wrinkles, and dries; death arrives and shakes all down, and what he leaves pays for what he sinned.
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly for batch completion; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: I Watch This Mountain January Ages
translations.text:
I watch this mountain January ages, and see its summit, gray with snow, decline while the chilled, dark, brief sun looks upon what it first painted.


I see the flattering sun indulge or drink its ice in many places, and grateful for its mercy the free, chattering musical crystal flows.


But in the Alps of your angry breast I do not see your fiery eyes indulge mine with the beloved ice.


My own flame multiplies the cold; frozen, I burn within my ashes, envying these rivers' happiness.
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly for batch completion; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: To Rome, Buried in Its Ruins
translations.text:
You seek Rome in Rome, O pilgrim, and in Rome itself you do not find her: the walls she displayed are a corpse, and the Aventine her own tomb.


Where the Palatine ruled, it lies; medals filed down by time show more the ravage of the ages' battles than Latin glory.


Only the Tiber remains; if its current once watered the city, now it mourns her as a grave with a doleful sound.


O Rome, in your greatness and beauty, all that was firm has fled; only the fleeting remains and endures.
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly for batch completion; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: I Embrace Fugitive Shadows
translations.text:
I embrace fugitive shadows; in dreams my soul grows weary; alone I wrestle night and day with a goblin held in my arms.


When I try to bind it tighter, it sees my sweat and slips away; I return more fiercely to my struggle, and stubborn love tears me apart.


I go to take revenge on a vain image that never leaves my eyes; it mocks me and runs proudly from its mockery.


I start to follow, but strength fails; and longing to reach it, I send my tears running after it in rivers.
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly for batch completion; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: He Drinks Fine Wine with Gnats Inside
translations.text:
German gnats of delicate sips, dandruff of the tastiest wine measures: because fire has moths, you want must to have wine-moths.


Winged wicks, petty atoms, drunken specks, vinous birds, envious fluff of wines, bees of bacon's honey.


Nits of the vintage, I admit you to my throat, since the grandson of the vine, blessed liquor, is your rope.


Sail with the swallow toward my Adam's apple; by drinking you all I repay the wine you drank, which drowns you.
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly for batch completion; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: In This Place Where May Encloses
translations.text:
In this place where May encloses all that blooms in most fruitful light, so like heaven it seems a piece of its globe fallen to earth,


the rocks of this range, shoulders offered to the celestial weight, witness the hard anguish my heart suffers in lofty bondage and unjust war.


I looked at the fountain where I used to see Phyllis gaze upon herself, when it stopped flowing to be her mirror.


Imitating my envy, it burned while my attention blazed in her hands; amid two fires, Phyllis froze.
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly for batch completion; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: A Pointed Woman in Petticoats
translations.text:
If you are a bell, where is the clapper? If a walking pyramid, go to Egypt; if an inverted top, bring an address; if a sugarloaf, I place you in Motril.


If a steeple, what are you doing below? If you are a penitent's badly contrite hood and crime, let the cypresses call you jay.


If an awl, why leave the case? If a dice cup, show your proof; if a dunce cap, fit yourself upon old women.


If Saint Anthony's sharp vision, call yourself Lady Funnel with tresses; if a woman, give those skirts to the devil.
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly for batch completion; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: No, Floralva, They Admit No Company
translations.text:
No, Floralva, ever-triumphant love and majesty admit no company: king and lover must stand alone; favor has monarchy's proud airs.


The burning father of daylight permits no presumptuous, sparkling star to show its face while he reigns in the empty region.


Love is so great a king that he binds heaven, sea, and earth in vassalage and boasts one sole majesty.


One heart encloses all his love; solitude is his crown's peace, company sedition and war.
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly for batch completion; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: To Aminta, Who Covered Her Eyes with Her Hand
translations.text:
What it takes from me in fire, the hand hiding your eyes gives me in snow; the whiteness that kills is no less cruel and stirs no lesser flames.


Sight drinks the fires fresh and spreads them like a volcano through the veins; the loving breast regards that whiteness fearfully, feeling it treacherous.


If you pass your hand across the tyrant ardor of your eyes to temper it, that is great pity for a human heart.


But not for you: though snow, your hand may melt when hiding it, unless your hand instead intends to freeze it.
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly for batch completion; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: Love Imprinted on the Soul, Enduring after Ashes
translations.text:
If my death were daughter to my love, what happy birth my love would bear against my life; what glory if dying sprang from loving!


Wherever I went I would carry in my soul the fire that burns me, and keep its faithful flame with cold ash in the very grave where I slept.


Beyond hard death my cares will live within my shade, and beyond Lethe my memory.


Your beauty will triumph over oblivion, my pure and burning faith over fate, and ceasing to be through love will be my glory.
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly for batch completion; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: Contradictions and Torments of His Love
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly for batch completion; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: He Blames Flor for Unjustly Rewarding Her Favor
translations.text:
Do you see the defeated bull groan at his disgrace, absent and shamed, the grove more clawed than grazed, and all the world wounded by his jealousy?


Do you see him rehearse revenge with bellows and spend armed force upon the wind? See that he feels disdain and knows his cow has another husband?


Then consider my pain, Flor, when for Corydon, an absent shepherd, you despise my company and love.


The cow offered herself to the bravest and rightly rewarded valor; you despise me unjustly, Flor.
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly for batch completion; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: Silent Waters Rain in Fleeces
translations.text:
Mute clouds rain silent waters in white fleeces; the day passes with majesty under cold shadow, while the hidden sun looks from balconies.


Hearts sustained by burning courage do not admit winter, for the Spanish monarchy pours equal strength into bulls and lances.


Jarama's glory, its broad brow wet and burning with grim rage, spills its purple life in blood.


Flattering Spain's great king, the snow-darkened storm applauded the arm, ash shaft, and cane.
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly for batch completion; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: Flora Ordered Me, Ah Fabio, to Love Her
translations.text:
Flora ordered me, ah Fabio, to love but not desire her; obedient, confused, and stained, my care adores her beauty without desiring it.


The enamored understanding enjoys in the eternal spirit, imprisoned in the mortal cloister that treasures it, what human passion feels and mourns.


To love is to know burning virtue; to desire is interested will, coarse, discourteous, and mortal.


The body is earth, will be earth, and was nothing; the mind proceeds from God to eternity: I am eternal lover of an eternal beloved.
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly for batch completion; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: Everywhere I Turn, I See
translations.text:
Everywhere I turn I see the threats of the burning flame; in every place I keep before me elusive torment and mocking desire.


Life is my prison, though I cannot believe it; to the sound of iron I forever drag and wet in absence, I try within myself to be Orpheus.


Furies and griefs inhabit my heart; there love is fire and tyrant, and within myself I suffer my own guilt.


O pitiless master who ordains this! Harmony is neither price nor ransom from punishment by an enemy hand.
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly for batch completion; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: That Color of Rose and Lily...
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly for batch completion; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: How Lazy the Feet, How Lingering
translations.text:
How lazy the feet, how lingering the steps death brings toward my harm; deceptions lengthen the road, and those already lost take scandal at me.


My eyes pretend not to understand; to mislead my disillusion, the years conceal truth and guard the senses' sleep.


At birth I came from womb to prison; from prison I will go loving to the grave, and in the grave I will always burn.


Every reprieve death gives me is mere delay that grows longer, so I may never finish dying in pain.
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly for batch completion; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: Love Sonnet
translations.text:
I embrace fugitive shadows; in dreams my soul grows weary; alone I wrestle night and day with a goblin held in my arms.


When I try to bind it tighter, it sees my sweat and slips away; I return with new strength to my struggle, and stubborn love tears me apart.


I go to take revenge on a vain image that never leaves my eyes; it mocks me and runs proudly from its mockery.


I start to follow, but strength fails; longing to reach it, I send my tears running after it in rivers.
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly for batch completion; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: Seneca
translations.text:
Seneca, answering your prepared argument suddenly today gives glory to your teaching, which has formed my tongue to speak eloquently against you.


Even what you have received from my hand is unworthy of what I owe you; for what I owe myself, it has only begun to reward you sparingly.


At the cost of my fame you want men to praise your modesty and restraint and accuse my greedy dropsy.


Enjoy the reward due my teaching, then, so that your returning it today and my refusing it may praise us both.
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly for batch completion; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.text:

I start to follow, but strength fails; longing to reach it, I send my tears running after it in rivers.

translations.title: He Compares the Concealment of His Tears
translations.text:
Either, Guadiana, your idle currents rest in lakes you ennoble, or in stormy rains you spread liquid fields for your fish;


or in thirsty, dark caves you make your watery torrents vanish, rejoicing to be born for Spain many times within cavernous tombs.


My two eyes, rivals of your springs, now run, now hide, now halt, and are born burning into tears without dying.


Neither my prison nor tears become clear: I wholly resemble your currents, sheltered by their own grave.
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly for batch completion; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: This Knotted Ivy That Climbs
translations.text:
This knotted ivy climbs and encloses in a green labyrinth the height of the poplar it harms, for all its caresses ruin it.


The eye, attending to the leafy lake, cannot decide whether it is embrace or prison; only the trunk knows whether it is favor or a jail that hides and bends it.


Ah, Lisi, whoever sees me enriched by lofty worship of your beauty and attended by such noble pains,


let him ask my passion and fortune, and learn that what he judges the glory of my madness is the prison of my senses.
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly for batch completion; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: Yesterday Was Dream, Tomorrow Will Be Earth
translations.text:
Yesterday was dream, tomorrow will be earth: shortly before, nothing; shortly after, smoke. I aim ambitions and presume, scarcely a point within the circle closing me.


A brief contest in troublesome war, I am the greatest danger in my own defense; while my weapons consume me, the body lodges me less than buries me.


Yesterday is gone, tomorrow has not arrived; today passes, is, and was, in motion that sends me plunging toward death.


Hour and moment are spades, hired by my pain and care to dig my monument within my life.
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly for batch completion; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: Lisi, You Will Find No Coolness in Shade
translations.text:
Lisi, you will find no coolness in shade, for with two burning lights you bring dog-day heat to shadow that could warm the Alps.


These places have made Daphne forget her ancient modesty and reserve; she who fled one sun feels safe from your two singular suns.


But seeing him divided in your eyes so he may dwell in you twice, she sees him twice defeated in you.


And she feels you hate him as she did, for you have withdrawn to her shade and trunk the rays you deny and offer him.
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly for batch completion; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: To Lope de Vega
translations.text:
Celebrated Pilgrim, the book that deserved, as yours, the respect of time and oblivion will shame their power.


The laurel, accompanied by bonds of gold and ivy, blushes beside your brow to see your writings make its rewards seem small.


Envy makes the name you win by song its executioner and torment, and its martyrdom grows with your glory.


Yet I excuse such boldness, if by biting your works it enriches mouth, tongue, and teeth.
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly for batch completion; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: He Rebukes an Adulteress for the Circumstances of Her Sin
translations.text:
In you alone, Lesbia, we see adultery lose its shame before Heaven, for licentious, free, and unveiled, you offend the sufferer's patience.


For God's sake, yours, mine, and your husband's, do not make his absence a public charge; shut the door and live cautiously, for sin prides itself on secrecy.


I do not say abandon your lovers; I say it is unwise for the few who are your enemies to know them.


Remember your offended neighbors say witnesses to your sins delight you more than the sins themselves.
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly for batch completion; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: On Violent and Unjust Prosperity
translations.text:
Maton alone now fills the litter, though only the day before yesterday the lean, gaunt informer barely cast a shadow and fit with room to spare in a mousetrap.


Today his house, badly introduced among the spheres, blocks the sun's steps and trips stars; once, had it been larger, it would have been a sty.


When he begged from all, we knew him; when he takes from all, he knows us not; today we cease to be what yesterday we gave.


He has in excess what Rome lacks; he cannot see us because we saw him: he hides what he was and displays what he usurps.
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly for batch completion; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: A Kitchen Maid Stood One January
translations.text:
A kitchen maid stood thigh-deep in the river one January, washing cloths with such spirit and vigor that she led a thousand fools by the nose.


A cheerful count asked her gracefully, “Are you cold?” The maid replied, “My lord, I always carry a brazier with me.”


The clever count, strutting like a peacock, asked her to light a candle he carried.


The maid raised her skirts to her backside and told him, “Then let your lordship blow this firebrand.”
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly for batch completion; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: You Waste Your Time, Death, on My Wound
translations.text:
You waste your time, death, upon my wound, for one who does not live suffers no death; if you must end my life, turn to those eyes where my life resides.


You dare not approach the sanctuary where it dwells withdrawn, pitiless though you are; if you saw it, you would become life and no longer know yourself.


I am ash left over from the flame; the fire left nothing to consume as it poured through love's blaze.


Turn to the wretch whose prayer calls you for rest from pain; I do not deny what I do not have.
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly for batch completion; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: If Gifts Break Hard Rocks
translations.text:
If gifts break hard rocks, the gift of your blood breaks and moves us, raining richly from your veins, fruitful love within your pure entrails.


Though we are soulless creatures who owe your pain as soul, we see the day pass dark and brief, and the sun behold dark hours within it.


Upon rock you built your Church and so ennobled our lineage that, God and man, you called yourself stone.


You postponed the claim to be bread; though you denied it to temptation, in the Sacrament you granted it in yourself.
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly for batch completion; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: To Apollo, Pursuing Daphne
translations.text:
Red-headed silversmith of the summits, by whose light the rabble picks off lice: if you want to enjoy the nymph Daphne, who flees in silence, pay and stop shining.


If you would save yourself grief, Eye of Heaven, arrange to buy her: Mars spent his armor on sweets, his sword on pastries and wine.


Stern Jupiter became a purse; the maiden raised her skirts to receive him as a rain of money.


It was some duenna-star's trick, for I infer no star goes without a duenna: Phoebus, since you are the Sun, make use of her.
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly for batch completion; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: Examples Show Flora Beauty's Brevity
translations.text:
The year's youth, the garden's ambitious blush, fragrant crimson ruby and shortened dart, also the year's lovely pride;


the rose's lush display, field's divinity and garden star, and the almond tree snowed in its own blossom, daring to anticipate the heat:


these, O Flora, silently rebuke beauty and human pride, which are subject to the laws of flowers.


Your age will pass while you doubt; tomorrow you will regret yesterday, and late, in pain, grow wise.
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly for batch completion; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: Vulcan Forged Them, Midas Touched Them
translations.text:
Vulcan forged them, Midas touched them: armor in which Mars is enclosed again, rigid with the mountain's price and discolored in golden metal.


Wounds followed the gesture when his arm shook the earth; the brush did not lend them—war gave them; Flanders saw them bloody and feared.


For what they bear of Girón of Osuna, their terrors know gentleness, and the Thracian moon is crimson upon them.


Their victorious faces thunder; Fortune aided Art in Guido, and the canvas is warlike in color.
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly for batch completion; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: Adam in Paradise, You in a Garden
translations.text:
Adam in Paradise, you in a garden; he placed in honor, you in agony; he sleeps and poorly watches his companion; yours sleep while you pray awake.


He committed the first disorder; you restored our first day; you drink the cup your Father sends, while he eats disobedience and lives dead.


The sweat of his face sustains him; yours sustains our glory; his was the guilt, yours the disgrace.


He left error, you leave remembrance; that was blind deceit, this redemption. How differently you leave our story!
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly for batch completion; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: On a Certain Lady at a Balcony
translations.text:
A certain lady at a balcony, with stocking and tight slipper, stirred the limp asparagus of a rough peasant spying on her.


When she noticed his gaze, she asked its cause; the peasant opened his heart and told what he saw and contemplated.


Raising an eyebrow, she said coyly, “Brother, this is merely seeing and desiring the fruit.”


The peasant drew out his tackle, took it in hand, and replied, “Then see and desire, madam whore!”
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly for batch completion; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: In Sicily There Is a Famous Spring
translations.text:
In Sicily a famous spring turns all it wets and bathes to stone; the light reed flees the vile rigor of its natural current.


From graceful foot to brow, Anaxarete was turned to stone by strange hardness; in Spain she could have offered a plainer example.


But where you are, there is no need to seek examples among creatures, since my complaints never softened you.


At last I am resolved to believe some mountain bore you from hard entrails, or you were baptized in this spring.
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly for batch completion; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: Since Today Grief Pours Night
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly for batch completion; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: Burdened with Myself, I See Ahead...
translations.text:
Burdened with myself, I see ahead death threatening my journey; persisting on the wrong path would show more folly than constancy.


If some foolish lover follows me to his harm—for misfortune never travels alone—ah, let him come to himself and turn back, not step where so blind a traveler stepped.


See how mistaken, lonely, sad, and disordered my road has been, a road no lost foot ever walked so.


For rather than retrace my path, seeing the feared end close ahead, I have sought it with steps from which others flee.
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly for batch completion; no separate editorial review was performed.
